$comment: Pinned source revision for the generated operation catalogs.
The catalogs are a published artifact: the paths and scopes in them are what the SDK
requests at runtime. Reading them from a moving branch means a rebuild can change client
behaviour with no corresponding change in this repository, and it makes CI non-reproducible.
So generation, `--check`, and CI all read this one file.
`ref` must be a full 40-character commit SHA. The generator warns loudly if it is a branch
name, because a branch is not a reproducible input.
`contractSha256` is the sha256 of `contractPath` (the content scope contract) at `ref`, as
qf-api-docs computes it (CRLF normalized to LF). Generation and `--check` fail when the pinned
revision's contract hashes to anything else, or when its `x-qf-scopes` metadata names a
different hash. The hash is recorded once per generated section, as the section's `contractSha256`.
To update: point `ref` at the approved qf-api-docs commit, set `contractSha256` to that
revision's contracts/content-scopes/v1.sha256 after reviewing the contract change, run
`pnpm --filter @quranjs/api generate:operation-catalogs`, and commit all three together.

Content scopes are resolved only on the `client_credentials` branch of `applyAuthHeaders`,
where `sub` equals the client id; the `user` branch sends the session's existing token
without choosing scopes at all. So `appCredentialsOnlyScopes` in the contract (granular
scopes that must not authorize a user-bound token) is enforced by the gateway, not here.
